# External Perplexity research: Scheidt's fourth process

External documentary synthesis, not an experiment.

## Published context
[Sanborn 2005](https://www.wired.com/2005/01/questions-for-kryptos-creator/) calls itself a partial transcript edited for length/organization; [Scheidt 2005](https://www.wired.com/2005/01/inside-info-on-kryptos-codes/) is edited likewise. Scheidt's sequence moves from “four different processes” to “all four (sections),” “first three parts,” and the “fourth part.” Best-supported reading: a high-level process per K1-K4: K1/K2 similar; K3/K4 different. A process can be a multi-operation pipeline, not four sequential K4 layers.

## Limits of masking evidence
Scheidt says all four sections are English; frequency/counting gave access to first-three English structure; he “disguise[d]” this in fourth; mask “may not be known.” This does not prove an unprecedented primitive, and does not identify fractionation, homophony, Bifid, Trifid, double transposition, Polybius, autokey, feedback, matrix multiplication, OTP, nulls, visual route, or multiple substitution layers. It supports stronger masking of ordinary English structure only.

## Roles
Scheidt: education, candidate historical/contemporary systems, modification ideas. Sanborn+Scheidt: thematic/story work. Sanborn: selection/final implementation and visual/material encoding. Scheidt did not necessarily inspect final engraving. Thus seek a Sanborn-modified pipeline, not one canonical unchanged Scheidt cipher.

## 2009 caution
[WIRED 2009](https://www.wired.com/2009/04/ff-kryptos/) mixes quotations and reporter synthesis. Late-19th-century-to-WWII methods, pencil-and-paper systems, polyalphabetic substitution, shifting matrices, and transposition are contextual synthesis unless direct quotes are recovered, not proof of K4 primitives.

## Candidate families
| Family | Permitted because | Weakened subsets | Open |
|---|---|---|---|
| Custom superencipherment | stronger mask; Sanborn modifications | narrow route/periodic/clock cases | layers/route/key/state |
| Long irregular polyalphabetic | K1/K2 precedent | periodic/progressive/feedback/direct-clock subsets | key/source/schedule |
| Fractionating coordinate/matrix | historically practical; indirect matrix evidence | small Trifid/fractionation subsets | square/period/alphabet/route |
| Homophonic/stateful | masks frequency | simple two-chart/low-order feedback | table/selector/reset |
| Semantic inner layer | Scheidt distinguishes external cipher/meaning | outer tests | plaintext/codebook |
